answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and put them face down at the bottom; shuffle all nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle all three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: Setup: shuffle/deal results in a face-down 10-card Conflict Deck; return unused Conflict cards without looking.

answers.answer: In four-player play, a human starts at 1 score; in three-player play, at 0. Both setups give two Agents on the Leader and a third (Swordmaster) beside the board, 3 troops in the garrison and 9 in supply, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: Score track on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader, third next to board; 3 troops in garrison, remaining nine in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain. After Revealing, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from your remaining hand, not cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, all cards from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Agent turns are optional; after Reveal your turns are skipped. Reveal Effects apply to just-revealed cards only; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: No: destination entry costs must be paid immediately before resolving any board-space or played-card effects, so an Agent-box effect cannot pay that entry. One card sends only one Agent, using one Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn and may only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs immediately before resolving effects; choose only one Agent icon; card with no Agent icons may only be revealed.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, all three troops recruited this turn may deploy, plus up to two additional troops from the four already in your garrison: at most five total. At a non-Combat space, troops cannot deploy and remain in the garrison. Recruited troops are taken from your supply and placed in the garrison first.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: troop recruitment takes a troop from supply into garrison; at a Combat space deploy any/all recruited this turn plus up to two more from garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy at a connected post to bypass another player's Agent at the destination, not your own. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card; choose immediately after placing your Agent, before receiving space or card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, though separate Spies can. You must still play an appropriate card for the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player's occupancy; Gather Intelligence choice is immediately after placement; cannot recall same Spy for both.

answers.answer: Strength is 11 (two troops at 2 each, one sandworm at 3, and four revealed swords at 1 each). If your last unit is removed, strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict, you may not participate in Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Strength: each troop 2, each sandworm 3, each revealed sword 1; if last unit removed strength is 0. Combat Intrigue requires at least one unit in Conflict.

answers.answer: Yes, you may act again after passing if an opponent plays a Combat Intrigue; the window closes when all players involved pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison) and sandworms to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: you are not required to pass because you passed earlier; resolve after consecutive passes. Cleanup returns troops to supply and sandworms to bank.

answers.answer: If two players tie for first in four-player play, each gets the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward, but nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. In a three-player game, tied first players each get second reward, no other reward is given, and nobody takes the card. A zero-strength player gets no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: exactly two tied first with four players means remaining players compete for third; nobody takes the card. Three or fewer tied first: second reward only. Zero strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; two sandworms do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards are not doubled. A reward offering 3 spice for 1 VP may be paid a second time under doubling: pay another 3 spice for another 1 VP, or 6 total spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more sandworms double; control and battle icons cannot; optional reward cost may be paid a second time, with example 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2.

answers.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card face up into your supply, check for another face-up Conflict or Objective card with a matching battle icon. If present, matching is mandatory: flip the pair face down for 1 VP. In Endgame, the wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply, flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win and take card, check face-up Conflict or Objective cards; must flip matching pair; during Endgame wild may match any icon.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP, lose it below 2, and regain it on reaching 2 again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained after falling below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; the first to 4 also gets the Alliance token and its 1 VP, which remains only while held. Tying the Alliance holder does not take it; gaining more Influence transfers it. If the holder loses Influence after having been tied, the FAQ says the formerly tied opponent takes it (or the former holder chooses among multiple tied opponents).
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: 2 Influence VP reverses below 2; 4 Influence has separate retained track bonus and Alliance VP; tying does not steal; FAQ gives transfer on holder losing Influence after tie.

answers.answer: Persuasion can be spent during Reveal before, between, or after Reveal effects. It may be pooled from multiple sources for one card or split across cards. The Imperium Row refills immediately to five, so you may acquire a replacement in the same Reveal if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: may use Persuasion before/between/after effects, pool or split; Row always has five and replacement may be acquired; acquired card goes face up to discard.

answers.answer: At Makers phase, add 1 spice to each Agent-free Maker space; when visiting a Maker space, take all accumulated bonus spice there. Summoning a sandworm places it directly in the Conflict, never in a garrison, and usually requires Maker Hooks if the effect specifies that prerequisite; Hooks are retained, not spent. While the Shield Wall remains, a worm cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin; removing the Wall permits summons to any Conflict. The summary says Hooks and Wall requirements depend on the particular summoning effect.
answers.evidence: Makers: add spice if space unoccupied; visit gains all. Sandworms: summon immediately to Conflict; specified Hooks prerequisite; Shield Wall protects three named locations; removal permits any Conflict.

answers.answer: At Recall, if anyone has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty, Endgame is triggered. Before comparing VP, players may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards. Most VP wins; ties break in order by spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring: at end of round threshold or empty deck triggers Endgame; first resolve Endgame Intrigue, then highest VP wins; listed tiebreakers.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup has two contracts face up and the rest of the standard 20 face down in the bank: 18 in bank without Shaddam, or 16 plus two set-aside Sardaukar contracts if Shaddam is chosen. Add four CHOAM Imperium cards and four CHOAM Intrigue cards. Shaddam is optional and usable only with CHOAM. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay in the box.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes: two face up; 20 standard, set aside two for Shaddam when chosen; add four additional Intrigue and four Imperium cards; contrasting-back set is Rise of Ix only.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of two face-up contracts and replace it from the bank; if players have taken all contracts, the icon instead gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes when you send an Agent to a Maker space and gain its stated spice amount that turn, including spice from other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts and Completing contracts: icon takes face-up contract and replaces; exhausted supply gives 2 Solari; definitions of Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire contracts.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space after already sending your Agent there this turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must hold the contract when sending the Agent. When completing a contract, announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: already-visited space contract waits until future turn; must have contract at placement; announce, gain rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. It receives the Ornithopter Objective; the other two eligible Objectives are dealt randomly to humans, and the human with the First Player marker on their Objective goes first. Turn order is First Player, Rival, other human; the Rival takes Agent turns while it has Agents and never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: one shared scoring Rival; Rival gets Ornithopter Objective; First Player determined from human card; order First Player → Rival → other human; Rival never Reveal.

answers.answer: A Rival ignores an occupied destination and reveals another House Hagal card until it can place on an unoccupied indicated space. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: use a free post of the specified type if one exists, otherwise ignore that placement; then reveal another Hagal card and continue the Agent turn. Rival ignores normal space costs and effects and applies only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue. The summary does not enumerate the costs and effects of every board space, but establishes they are ignored for the Rival.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: occupied destinations ignored and reveal again; Place Spy no Agent and reveal another; ignores normal space costs/effects; reshuffle immediately.

answers.answer: Omit Objective cards whose player-count marking does not match, shuffle eligible cards, and distribute one face up to each player. The Objective marked with the First Player marker determines the human First Player; in standard three- and four-player setup the summary gives no more specific Objective selection procedure beyond matching the count and random distribution. Shaddam cannot be chosen without CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit mismatched Objective cards, shuffle and deal face up; marked Objective determines First Player. Shaddam is not used unless playing with CHOAM.

answers.answer: The bank's Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; use any convenient substitution if they run out. Troops are different: if your personal supply has no troops, you cannot recruit more until troops return to it. Resource gains come from the bank and payments return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup bank: resources and sandworms not meant to be limited; substitute as needed. Recruit from supply; if empty cannot recruit; gain from bank and payments return to bank.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict card and each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, players recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Player Reference: ordered phases; Round Start reveals Conflict and draws five; Recall prepares next round by recalling Agents and passing First Player.

answers.answer: Yes. Space effects, played card Agent-box effects, and the Faction Influence advance may be resolved in any order. No: the entry cost and requirements must be met immediately before resolving any space or card effects, so Influence gained from the visit cannot satisfy that visit's requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs and meet requirements immediately before effects; gain space and Agent-box effects and Faction Influence; may carry out all effects in any order.

answers.answer: No. An optional arrow cost and effect can be paid and gained only once per turn, except sandworm doubling of a Conflict reward. Most card and space effects are mandatory; exceptions include 'may,' optional arrow costs, and optional black-X trash. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play it; all costs must be paid. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card directs you to trash itself.
answers.evidence: Arrows: may pay/gain only once per turn except doubled Conflict rewards. FAQ: most effects mandatory with stated exceptions; Intrigue costs/conditions must be met. Trashing section explains exceptions.

answers.answer: A Spy may be placed from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spies in supply, you may first recall one for no effect. If the placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type that must connect to the post, you may only place at a post connected to that icon; otherwise you cannot place the Spy.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: place on unoccupied post; may recall one if none in supply; some effects require a particular Agent icon connected to post.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate cannot bypass your own Agent. A Spy may be recalled without playing a card for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence, but the recall still requires playing a card for the Agent turn and does not waive costs or requirements. No, you cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; two Spies may be recalled for different effects, one to Infiltrate and one to Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Infiltrate only bypasses another player; FAQ says recall requires card for Agent turn; cannot use two to Gather Intelligence, but may use one for each different effect.

answers.answer: A controller gains its listed bonus whenever any player, including the controller, visits Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Winning the corresponding Conflict places your Control marker, replacing an opponent's marker. When the Conflict is revealed for a space you control, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to Conflict.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations: controller receives bonus whenever any player visits; winning sets/replaces control marker; defensive bonus is one troop from supply.

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the first-place winner keeps the first reward and card, and no further rewards are given. Players tied for third receive nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward, nobody takes the Conflict card, and no other rewards are given, including to a remaining fourth player.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tie for second earns third reward for each; tie for third gets nothing. Three tied first gives second reward to each and no other rewards in either player count.

answers.answer: In a normal three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second place receive their rewards and third receives nothing. This is also true when the Rival is a participant in a two-human-plus-Rival game: ordinary first and second rewards are paid, third gets nothing except in a tie for second.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: with two or three players ordinary first and second receive rewards, third nothing; explicitly includes two humans plus Rival.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigue may be played at any point on your own Agent or Reveal turns; Combat Intrigue only during Combat and only if you have a unit in Conflict; Endgame Intrigue only at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, and reveal only when played; after resolving, place face up in discard next to Intrigue Deck. If that deck runs out, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards: timing by type, storage and discard; FAQ says if Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle discard to form new deck.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard cannot be an Intrigue unless the instruction specifies Intrigue. Ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand. Secrets steals one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigue cards.
answers.evidence: Discarding: from hand, not in play/discard; cannot be Intrigue unless specified. Secrets: opponents with four or more give one selected at random.

answers.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or the card directs you to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove VP already gained from its acquire effect.
answers.evidence: Trashing section lists eligible zones and destinations; FAQ says Spice Must Flow acquire VP is retained if card is later trashed.

answers.answer: Acquire-box effects resolve once at the moment you acquire the card. When a draw is needed and your deck is empty, reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion cannot carry over; it is lost at the end of your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquire box resolves at acquisition; acquiring cards says reshuffle discard when unable to draw; unused Persuasion is lost.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on your Reveal turn are in play and remain face up through Clean Up, unless trashed first. Two Fremen Bond cards can activate one another regardless of play order. They cease being in play when moved to the discard pile during Clean Up.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: both kinds of cards remain in play until Clean Up; two Bond cards activate one another regardless of order.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just placed this turn. The recalled Agent can be used on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop goes from Conflict to your garrison. 'Retreat any number' permits zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon returns another Agent and may be used again same round; Retreat sends troop to garrison; FAQ says retreat any number allows zero.

answers.answer: No. When a freely chosen Influence effect grants two, choose one Faction and gain both Influence there. An Alliance-icon effect requires holding that Faction's Alliance token; a minimum-Influence effect requires meeting its stated Influence threshold.
answers.evidence: Influence: freely chosen gain two cannot choose two different Factions; Alliance icon requires holding token; some effects require minimum Influence.

answers.answer: If the Alliance holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if several opponents were tied, the former holder chooses which gets it. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more, return the Alliance token to the board and the holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: Official FAQ—Alliance loss: formerly tied player takes token; among several tied former holder chooses; if holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return it to board.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the five cards drawn then. A Plot Intrigue played earlier whose effect applies at Reveal stays face up until that Reveal effect is used, then is discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Draw timing: drawn during Reveal means immediately reveal and use this turn; drawn after Reveal means keep for next round; Plot Intrigue with later Reveal effect stays face up until then, is used, then discarded.
